title: Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin methods for scattering by periodic structures: the explicit stability estimate away from Rayleigh--Wood anomalies (Theorem 3.5)
author: Armando Maria Monforte, Andrea Moiola
work: Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin methods for scattering by periodic structures
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem printed as Theorem 3.5 of "Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin methods for scattering by periodic structures" (source0.tex lines 883--890, source label thm-stima), delivered together with the article's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 891--1101 (211 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is the paper's advertised new result: for the quasi-periodic Helmholtz transmission problem in a bounded cell with Dirichlet-to-Neumann boundary conditions it gives the fully explicit stability bound ||kappa u||_{L2(Omega)}^2 + ||grad u||_{L2(Omega)}^2 <= 10 L kappa_+ |sin theta| ( (H/delta) ||kappa||_{L-infinity(Omega)}^2 (2+7H max{kappa^+,kappa^-})^3 + 1 ), valid under the article's non-trapping assumption and whenever the wavenumber stays away from Rayleigh--Wood anomalies by a margin delta>0. The proof is complete inside the retained span: it expands the solution in the outgoing Fourier series on the two artificial boundaries, invokes the article's own well-posedness theorem to know that the solution exists and is unique, splits u into Fourier coefficients on Gamma_{+-H}, uses the Rellich identity together with the sign properties of the real and imaginary parts of the DtN operators to eliminate the evanescent modes, controls the propagating modes by the non-anomaly margin delta, bounds the boundary L2 norms, and finishes with a Poincare-type inequality in the vertical direction and an explicit bookkeeping of the constants down to the constant 10L kappa_+ |sin theta| of the statement. It is not a routine exercise: it combines a Rellich/Pohozaev multiplier identity, the spectral sign structure of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators, a non-trapping geometric assumption and a uniform-in-parameter constant tracking, and it reproduces the paper's headline estimate. Rated H3 because the delivered unit is the article's main theorem and the argument is research-level analysis (explicit stability for a Helmholtz transmission problem at and away from Rayleigh--Wood anomalies) rather than anything found in an ordinary PhD qualifying syllabus; it is above H2 because the constant in the estimate has to be tracked through the whole chain and the Rayleigh--Wood anomaly degeneracy has to be handled by the explicit margin delta.
